thread.title: Investing in chip technologies tied to smartphones always co

author: Stephen Simpson, CFA
title: Investing in chip technologies tied to smartphones always co
text:
Investing in chip technologies tied to smartphones always comes with certain risks, including serious price erosion, rampant competition, and the risk that your customers will eventually replace you with their own internally-developed chips. Even so, Austria's ams AG ( OTCPK:AMSSY ) (AMS.S) looks to be worth a closer look on the basis of the company's strong integrated approach to 3D sensing and opportunities to generate growth in areas like industrial/auto, audio, and environmental sensing on top of significant opportunities in handset-based 3D sensing.
3D Sensing The Next Big Thing Building in part on its strength in light sensors (ams has long supplied handset companies like Apple ( AAPL ) and Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) with ambient light sensors) and multiple acquisitions, ams has assembled strong capabilities in 3D sensing - one of the strongest emerging new opportunities in semiconductors. 3D sensing can detect image patterns, distance, and shape, allowing for a wide range of uses, including facial recognition, augmented reality, machine vision, robotics, and LIDAR.
While there are many rivals along the component chain, ams is unusual in its integrated approach - offering a light source (VCSEL), controlling optics (including wafer-level optics), image sensors, and modules - and it presents itself as a "one-stop shop" for 3D sensing. Although ams is not currently present in the software side, the company has recently begun investing in software development as a way to spur future adoption. Ams has also recently begun a collaboration with Sunny Optical , a leading Asian sensor manufacturer, to take advantage of Sunny's capabilities in module manufacturing.
